column1: # HOTD2 global data labels — the committed source of truth for the Ghidra database.
# Windows TEB fields and resource labels are excluded: Ghidra creates those itself.
# **Rows are sorted by address, and every writer must keep them that way.**
# tools/annotate.py inserts in order; ExportAnnotations.java re-sorts on write.
# The file used to be append-only and grouped into topical sections, and both
# workstreams appending at the tail is where every TSV merge conflict came
# from -- two branches adding unrelated rows to the same last line. Sorted
# insertion puts them in different parts of the file instead. The sections
# went with it: each one spanned nearly the whole segment, so address order
# broke the twelve of them into 149 fragments.

column3: jump targets for spawn class 0x33
byte index into the targets; valid selectors 1-11 and 99

u32[41], the arm addresses PlaceGenericProp's switch jumps to, indexed by g_place_generic_prop_arm_index[type - 6]. Nine of the arms write obj+0x28C with an immediate (types 6, 10, 13, 19, 34, 56 and 67), one computes it (type 43's 0x19E8-or-0xFFFF at 0x00462330) and five re-write it from the placer's own +0x11C, which is the prologue's value again and not an overwrite. That distinction is the second clause of the descriptor-slot rule in tools/verify_prop_pose.py: a type whose arm takes the field away from the descriptor cannot have the descriptor naming its model.

u8[0x48], the byte index table of PlaceGenericProp's type switch: 0x00461DA2 loads the descriptor's type from placer+0x130C, subtracts 6, refuses anything above 0x47, indexes this, and jumps through g_place_generic_prop_arms. So types 6..77 have an arm and types 5 and 78 fall to the default at 0x004628CE -- which is why PropDrawOnlyType5's obj+0x28C is the prologue's untouched and it has no per-type setup at all. 72 entries selecting 41 distinct arms, so most arms serve more than one type. tools/verify_prop_pose.py walks it to decide which arm a type's slot and lifetime writes belong to.
8 entries; entries 6 and 7 share a target

u32[2][4][5], the factory pad masks per player and binding set: player 0 {4,0,0,0,2} gun, {4,0x4002,0x400,0x8000,0} controller, {4,2,1,0x400,0}, {4,2,0,0,0}; player 1 the same shifted 16. So the trigger is A (0x4) everywhere, the reload is B (0x2, Right Ctrl on the PC keyboard) on a pad, and a gun has NO reload bit: it reloads by shooting off the screen. [proved]

f64 0x3F1921FB54442D18 = 2pi/65536 exactly -- BAMS to radians, and a DOUBLE: MatrixRotateX/Y/Z are FILD angle; FMUL double [here]; FSTP float, so the radians they use are the double product rounded to float, not a float constant. 155 readers. PropUpdateType35 (0x0046B320) keeps the product on the FPU into FSIN, so it sees the double. web/src/core/bams.ts carries both (BAMS_TO_RAD, BAMS_TO_RAD_F64).
f64 0x40C45F306DC9C883 = 32768/pi, radians to BAMS -- the reciprocal of g_bams_to_rad beside it. MatrixInterpolateSwingTwist multiplies both FPATAN results by it before __ftol.
10.0f. RegisterForCameraTracking's sort key is the distance from the camera eye times this, as an int.

Four {f32 dx, f32 dy, f32 scale, u32 id} CreditPromptDrawCount reads at fixed offsets: 0 CREDIT(S) 0x22E (32, 15, 0.85), 1 FREE PLAY 0x332 (34, 15, 0.85), 2 and 3 only their dx -- 82 to the tens digit, 12 on to the units. [proved]

u8[16], bone -> destroyed-zone bit index for obj+0x1318. char_adv00: bone 2 (head) -> 0, bones 3-5 (right arm) -> 1, bones 6-8 (left arm) -> 2, all others 0xFF -- the shift is masked with 0x1F so those land harmlessly on bit 31.

One float per character type, copied to obj+0x124 by EnemyZombieInit, EnemyThrowerInit, CivilianInit (0x0048A6DC), ScriptedHumanoidInit (0x004841F7), OneHitTargetInit (0x00448F76) and the class-0x21 handler (0x00451780) -- six classes, so obj+0x124 is ONE field with one meaning across every class that sets it, and is not polymorphic. Index 7 is 10.0 and indices 1..6 are 15.0. Paired with the separate dword obj+0x128, a per-class authored constant: 1.0 for a class-0x10 civilian (CivilianInit 0x0048A433 loads 0x3f800000 into EDI, 0x0048A6D6 stores it), 3.5 for the zombie (CivilianInit 0x0048A7DF writes 0x40600000 onto each child it builds), and 5.0 for thrower type 0x16 or 4.0 for types 0x17-0x19. The two are written by adjacent instructions in one basic block, which is the proof they are two fields and not an overlay. obj+0x128 is also the radius class 0x10's op 0x16 ramp walks.
per character: u16[bone][6], the asset slot the bone is redrawn with after each successive hit
per character: u16[bone][6], damage for each successive hit on that bone. char_adv00's head runs 100/120/140/160
u16[16], bone -> hit-reaction group. Eight groups partitioning the body: 1 head, 2 torso, 3 right arm (bones 3-5), 4 left arm (6-8), 5 pelvis (9), 6 right leg (10-12), 7 left leg (13-15).

29 pointers, one per effect id, to the root node of that effect's part tree: {u32 asset slot; s16 bone index; u16 child count; u32 children[]}. Same shape as g_character_skeletons but with no bind offsets -- an effect's translations come per-frame from its motion. Bounded by g_effect_bone_counts at 0x004D5404: 0x74 / 4 = 29 entries, and every tree's node count matches its bone count.

s16 per effect id: how many nodes its tree has, INCLUDING the root, and therefore n-1 bones of animation data. EffectFrameTranslations and EffectFrameRotations both derive the motion stride from it as (n * 0x12 - 0xF) & ~3 -- truncating, not rounding up -- so one frame is (n-1) translations of three floats followed by (n-1) rotations of three BAMS shorts. Effects 2 and 3 are 3 nodes each and motion 471's block strides 36 bytes, which is that formula exactly.

u8 per effect id, the rate EffectPoseNode samples at. 0 reads one key per play frame. 1 and 2 halve it -- key = cursor / 2, blended half way toward key + 1 on odd cursors -- and 2 additionally slerps through matrices when any of the three angles differs by more than 0x3000. Effects 2 and 3 are mode 1.
0.01f. A circular ripple's amplitude scales by max(0, 1 - r * this), so it dies at 100 units.
char type -> skeleton block; count at +0x16, node pointers at +0x18
char type -> bones in a motion frame; one more than the top bone index

motion id -> the clip clock the scripts compare against, s16 per id. NOT the frame count: the animation clock ticks once per 60 Hz frame over data authored at 30 Hz, so across the 220 motions the bundles bake it is 2n-2 for 91 and 2n-3 for the other 129 and never anything else. Every cue expressed in clip frames is in these units -- ZombieStateTargetMotionScript's kill frame, ZombieStateMotionCue21's exit, the class-0x25 VM's -1 for the last frame, class 0x24's 0x32 drift cue. Comparing them against the authored frame count loses every cue past halfway.

Ids 0x00-0x23 are all bone 2 and name a hito_kao_*/etc_*_kao head, which ActorBindPartList swaps in for the skeleton's own; ids 0x24-0x50 name an etc_komono_* accessory on bone 2 (hair and hats), bone 1 (bags and aprons) or bones 12 and 15 (shoes), which ActorDrawAttachedParts draws in addition. kao = face, komono = small accessory.

u32 per player: the shot the gun makes. PlayerFireAndReloadUpdate plays g_gunshot_sound_ids[player] at the trigger, right after PlayerShotEffectSpawn, and PlayerFireOriginalModeWeapon falls back to it whenever the equipped weapon has no sound of its own -- which is every weapon in the shipped build, because g_original_weapon_sound_kind is seeded 0 and index 0 of g_original_weapon_gunshot_ids is 0. The two values are a9163400 a9163300: 0x003416A9 is COMMON\GUN5_22.WAV for player 0 and 0x003316A9 is COMMON\GUN4_22.WAV for player 1. A dry trigger plays nothing at all -- with the magazine empty the routine goes to PlayerRefillMagazine instead, which plays 0x3E16A9 COMMON\RELOAD1_44.WAV while the firing gate is open.

Bounded by g_original_weapon_reload_ids starting at 0x004EC9C0, not by a terminator. Entry 0 is 0, which is the fall-back to g_gunshot_sound_ids; 1..7 are DC_SE\SHOT_GUN_22, MCHN_GUN_22, GRENADE_22, MAGNUM_22, AIR_GUN_22, TOY_GUN1_44 and RULE3_22. The order agrees with g_original_weapon_kind's own arms -- 3 is the grenade that draws no muzzle flash, 4 the magnum, 5 the air gun.

Only two entries are set: 3 is DC_SE\GR_REL_22.wav for the grenade and 5 is DC_SE\AIR_G_REL_22.wav for the air gun; the other six are 0 and take COMMON\RELOAD1_44.WAV. float[11][2], {x, y} per damage overlay kind, added to the camera-space translate in DamageOverlayUpdateAndDraw. All 22 are 0.0 in the shipped exe. Extent bounded by the index (kind 0..10, FLD [kind*8 + 0x4ECAD8]) and by g_damage_overlay_scales starting exactly after. [proved]

float[2][2], [player count - 1][player]: 0, 0, then -0.22, +0.22. The code indexes 0x004ECB54 + (player + g_max_attackers*2)*4 with a count of 1 or 2, so the first two words it could name belong to g_damage_overlay_scales and are never read. With two players the overlays sit left and right of centre. [proved]

Five s32 per part. The first four are the bones the part's four VERTEX GROUPS are pulled toward; the fifth is the bone whose matrix the whole part is drawn in -- DrawCharacterPartSlot sets the matrix from it and DeformCharacterPartGroup pre-multiplies by its inverse, so the two cancel and a vertex lands at group_bone_matrix * source. A group whose bone equals the fifth therefore deforms to the identity, which is why the group-0-only drawer is correct for a part whose other group is the draw bone's. Default part 0 is {1,1,9,0} drawn at 9 -- upper body and pelvis, the waist. Part 1 is {9,9,10,13} drawn at 9 -- pelvis and both thighs, a skirt. Per-character-type tables replace it for 0x0E (0x004ED348), 0x1F/0x46/0x4E (0x004ED4B0), 0x41 (0x004ED780), 0x4C (0x004ED618) and 0x53 (0x004ED8E8).
Per character type, a pointer to an array of draw routines, one per entry in that type's g_pCharacterExtraParts list. DrawCharacterPart calls g_character_part_drawers[char_type][i](i).
Eight records for character type 0x17's part 1, stride 0x10: {s32 bone; s32 asset_slot; u32 mesh_info; u32 draw_info}. Read only by BuildCharacterPartSubparts.

{u32 count; u32 *descriptors[]} per character type -- the VERTEX-BLENDED parts, which are not in the skeleton because they are not rigid to one bone. BuildCharacterPart makes each one a private copy of the model's vertex buffer and re-transforms up to four groups of its vertices by four different bone matrices every frame (g_character_part_bones), then draws the whole slot in a fifth bone's space. 68 of 76 types have one or two; the cat has none. Part 0 is the waist, which spans the upper body and the pelvis, and without it a humanoid has a hole there. Part 1 is the skirt, over the pelvis and both thighs -- its slot is the PELVIS MODEL ITSELF, and SkeletonNodeDrawSuppressed is what stops bone 9 also drawing it rigidly.

33.0, shared rather than boss-specific: Class14ApplyBoneDamage and Boss4ResolveShot both cap on it. Class14ApplyBoneDamage multiplies g_class14_bone_damage only in g_GameMode 1 (Original) -- x2 when the player's g_original_item_slots factor at +0x0C is -1.0, else x that factor (0x00476772..0x00476795) -- and takes the table value unmultiplied in Arcade Mode, then the smaller of that and this.

s8 {x, z} [5]: the wander grid's cell size. Target = origin + base - cell*4 + rand()%(cell+1) + column*cell.

RegisterForDistanceRank has exactly one caller in the whole binary -- EnemyZombieUpdate at 0x0045346D -- so the queue holds class-0x30 actors and nothing else, and obj+0x131D/0x131E are written only onto those.

The distance-rank queue: 14 pairs of {u32 key, actor*} at stride 8, key at +0x00 and the actor pointer at +0x04 (0x005A4D5C). The key is |actor.xz - camera.xz| scaled by g_camera_track_key_scale and converted with __ftol, so it is a u16 -- which is why SortEnemiesByDistance radix-sorts it in exactly two 8-bit passes. RankEnemiesByDistance's second pass nulls the pointer of any entry that is not live or that carries obj+0x34 bit 0x20000000, and its third pass numbers the survivors into obj+0x131E.
{u32 distance key; void *actor} pairs, at most 14, radix-sorted nearest-first before the slots are assigned.

SortEnemiesByDistance's ping-pong buffer: the {key, actor*} pairs are counted into a 256-bucket histogram, scattered here, and copied back to g_distance_rank_list, once per 8-bit digit. Not read anywhere else.

The two dwords ActorPlayHitVoice's kind 4 reads -- 0x005A4EA8 for voice set A and 0x005A4EAC for set B. BOTH ARE ZERO IN THE IMAGE AND NOTHING WRITES THEM: the only two references in the whole binary are the reads at 0040A849 and 0040A852, a byte search for the little-endian address finds one instruction, and no call site anywhere passes 4. The nearest writer that could reach them is the {key, actor} scratch buffer SortCameraCandidates and SortEnemiesByDistance share at 0x005A4E38, whose 14 entries end at 0x005A4EA7 -- one dword short -- and both feeders are capped at 14 (g_camera_candidates, and RegisterForDistanceRank's CMP ESI,0xE). So kind 4 reaches PlaySoundId(0), which early-outs. Kind 4 plays nothing.
What CameraImpulseShakeTick adds to g_camera_eye each frame of a push: dir * 8.0 (0x004C43A0) * 1/15 (0x004D1CE4) at the start, plus g_camera_impulse_velocity every frame. [proved]

The REQUESTED application state, -1 for none. RequestAppState (0x0040E850) writes it, ClearPendingAppState (0x0040E840) and CommitAppState (0x0040E860) reset it to -1. Recomputed once per frame at the top of EvtInterpreterLoop and read by nothing else: 'may the script advance'. Every wait opcode 0x40..0x47 tests it before it lets the script on, so on the continue screen the script stands at the wait it had reached while the scene runs on under it; wait_frames (0x42) keeps counting down and passes on the first live frame. The extra frame wait_enemies_alive costs. Used ONLY by EvtOpWaitEnemiesAlive44 -- 0045FC42 reads it, 0045FC4B and 0045FC60 write it, and those three are every reference in the program. The handler requires 0 < it before it will pass, zeroes it when it does, and increments it on every frame it does not. It is NOT reset when the count condition fails, so it does not mean 'the g_enemies_alive condition must hold for two consecutive frames' -- an earlier note here said that and it is wrong. It means 'this instance of the instruction must already have been evaluated once and refused'. On top of g_evt_yield's first-visit yield that makes 0x44 the only wait in the VM that cannot pass before its third frame on the program counter; 0x43 is the same handler without this term and costs two.

s32[2], one per player, stride 4 -- not bytes; DAT_009A2BA4 is element 1. 0 is free and the claim stores 1: the entry says a permit is out, not who has it. An approaching enemy must claim one through TryClaimAttackSlot before it may attack, so only g_max_attackers enemies commit at a time. The holder's index is kept in obj+0x121, and SelectCameraLookAtTarget focuses the camera on whoever holds one. Class 0x31 state 27 bypasses the claim and writes the slot itself. EvtActionFinishSequence21 zeroes BOTH at 0x00403714/0x0040371E on every finish_sequence, whoever holds them -- which is what frees a ZombieStateHoldForCameraCue captor that graduated on its cue frame holding one. [proved]

s32, one of the three counters FUN_0040E730 steps once a game tick beside g_frame_counter (0x009A32A0) and g_blink_frame_counter (0x009A5C50). What distinguishes it: ResetSceneOnEnter (0x0045EDD0) zeroes it at 0x0045EE23 with EBX, which XOR EBX,EBX made 0 at the top -- so it counts TICKS SINCE THE SCENE WAS ENTERED. FUN_0040A920 zeroes it on a new game and the save path (FUN_0049F780 / FUN_0049F380) stores and restores it with the other two. Nothing else writes it, and FUN_0046EEE3 tests it == 0 to mean the scene's first tick, which only works if that is what it holds. Every other reader uses it as an ANIMATION PHASE: PropDrawOnlyType31 %% 7 into slot 0x1797, PropDrawOnlyType53 %% 15 into 0x135F and & 7 into 0xB67, FUN_0046B480 %% 0x18 into 0x161B, FUN_00467F50 %% 0x28 as a once-every-40-ticks gate, FUN_00469C80 * 0x180 as a sine phase.

The event VM's STEP index -- not a block counter and NOT monotonic. EvtAdvanceStepOrRoute increments it at the top and assigns it 1 in the route branch, so it runs 1..k within a block and drops back to 1 on a block change; FUN_0045EBC0 seeds it with 0, 1 or 5 by game mode. Class 0x41 and 0x44 props age one tick every time it CHANGES (PropExpireByStepLifetime), which makes obj+0x11C a lifetime in STEPS. Blocks average 3.99 steps, so reading it as a block count makes props live about four times too long. A block with one live step goes 1 -> 1 across its transition and does not age a prop at all.

Written only by EvtOpSetSceneLighting14 (and zeroed by SceneLightArrayInit). While non-zero, SceneLightArrayUpdate builds and submits the light array, and every draw routine that tests it -- RegionDrawResidentSet for draw_mode 1, DrawCharacterPartSlot on obj+0x38 bit 3, ZombieSubmitSlotByLighting on obj+0x136C bit 0x20 (TEST byte ptr [EAX+0x136c], CL with CL = 0x20 at 0x00453AE7 -- not obj+0x38, as this row used to say; EnemyZombieInitByCharType raises obj+0x38 bit 3 from that same bit), ThrowerDrawPart and ThrowerDrawPartWithAlpha on obj+0x136C bit 0 -- submits through SubmitSlotWithSceneLightArray, or its faded twin AssetDrawSlotWithAlphaSceneLights. CivilianInit raises obj+0x38 bit 3 when it is set at spawn.
The run's CONTINUE? countdown (RunPhaseContinueArm / RunPhaseContinueCountdown): 0x9FFF, -0x2D a frame, digit >> 12. [proved]

The event block currently executing, written by EvtAdvanceStepOrRoute and recorded byte-wise into g_route_history. NOT g_evt_step_index (0x009A2BB0), which is the step index within the current block and is what prop lifetimes measure. It is ALSO how a stage hands the next stage its starting point: on the scene-over path EvtAdvanceStepOrRoute writes it from the terminal route record's next[0], and nothing between there and FUN_0045EBC0 -- not AdvanceToNextScene, not LoadSceneAndReset, not ResetSceneOnEnter -- touches it again.
f32, stride 0xC, one per ring set. The middle radius; see g_enemy_approach_rings.
f32, stride 0xC, one per ring set. The outer radius; see g_enemy_approach_rings.

Ten bytes, one per Boss Mode entry, saturating at 5. BossModeRecordGrade (0x00425F40) returns at once unless g_GameMode == 3 and otherwise increments the entry at DAT_009A2268 -- or the second byte of the pair at 0x009A2C18 when DAT_009A2BBC == 1 and the index is 8 -- while the achieved rank DAT_009C8FB0 is at least the stored value and no more than 4. All ten at 5 bumps DAT_009C90C6/D3/DD; all ten non-zero ORs 4 into DAT_009C9F5E. Copied into the 0x009C9F33 save block alongside g_original_items_taken. That there are TEN of them against six scenes is [open].

Four dwords, and the only thing that lets a class-0x51 fish leave the surface -- FishClaimSlotAndLunge claims one and gives up when all four are taken, so four fish can be in the air and no more. The index is also WHERE the fish leaps to: the four are points in the camera's own space at x = +/-1.5, z = -6.0, with the odd two 2.0 lower, and in a two-player game 0 and 1 belong to player 0. A class-0x51 group header (tail+0x0E == 6) clears all four, as do Class14StateSummonRoundA's sub 0 and Class14StateSummonRoundB's, and SpawnWaterEnemyAt refuses to place a fish while any one is set.
Gates the g_rank_clock increment in the run-phase frame; ResetDamageRank sets it to 1. [proved]

Per player (stride 0x1C) the last world impact: point +0x00..0x08, surface +0x0C, normal +0x10..0x18. SpawnWorldImpact writes it; Boss4ResolveShot reads a mesh bone's point and surface from it. [proved]

The object a carried actor rides. CarrierPropSelectRoutine writes it at 0x0044019A -- the only write get_xrefs_to lists; readers CivilianInit, CarriedZombieInit18, Boss4Init. (An earlier row said Class26Subtype2Update writes it too: it does not, 0x0048EB1C writes g_carrier_object 0x009A5C34.) CarriedZombieInit18 copies it to obj+0x13B0 at spawn, so every rider placed after a carrier belongs to that carrier. It is read at spawn time only, which is why the script places the boat and its passengers in the same instruction -- and why a port that spawns the boat after its passengers (as the player did, slot actors after character spawns) seats them on no carrier.

Outstanding queued actions. +1 per queue_event (evt 0x30); every action handler does -1 when it completes -- EXCEPT EvtActionFinishSequence21 (selector 0x21), which installs a persistent camera driver and pins g_evt_action_advance at 0, so it never retires itself. evt 0x31/0x32 (goto_scene_state) and 0x33 (set_action_drain_mode, always delta -1) are its script-side retirement, and evt 0x40 blocks while this is non-zero. MEASURED: all 316 goto_scene_state sites in the shipped evt files have exactly one outstanding unretired queue_event 0x21 at that point. FUN_0045EBC0 zeroes it per block, so an imbalance cannot accumulate past a block boundary.
per player, 0x68 bytes: world ray origin, direction, -pitch/-yaw and their sin/cos

The projection distance in pixels, float. Its one writer is SetupSceneProjection at 0x0041853B: FLD double [0x004ED1D0] = 0.35866388296751145 (20.55 degrees, half the 41.1-degree vertical field), FPTAN, FDIVR float [0x004C49C8] = 240.0 -- so 240 / tan(20.55 deg) = 640.2079, the half-height of a 480-line frame over the tangent. ActorIsOnScreen, BuildShotRay, ThrowerPickLandingPoint and the screen-sprite spawners divide by it. [proved]
the cp_ slot currently playing; gates most object rigs
int[2], per player: the bone index this player's shot hit. DispatchHit copies it from (s8)obj+0x190+player before calling ResolveHit.
free-running, incremented once per frame; NOT the cam path frame
s32: the lives a new game (or a continue) starts with. FUN_0040AB50 = g_start_lives_by_option[0x009C9F21]; read only by PlayerEnterPlay. [proved]

Set by BOTH claim functions when the actor they are about to grant a permit to is OFF SCREEN -- ActorIsOnScreen returns 0 -- and read first by both, which gives up before a player is even picked. So one enemy may be attacking unseen and while one is, nobody else may claim at all. Cleared by ReleaseAttackSlot, ThrowerReleaseAttackPermit and ZombieStateHoldAtRange, each gated on the actor's own bit: obj+0x136C bit 0x20000 for class 0x30, bit 0x8000 for class 0x31 -- the hub only while the actor is still off screen (0x00455748..0x0045576D). Also cleared unconditionally by EvtOpQueueEvent30 when it QUEUES a selector-0x21 finish_sequence (0x0045F833), and by ZombieStateStandAndThrow (0x00459361). Being off screen does NOT refuse the claim. [proved]

4 records of 16 bytes {f32 strength; f32 x, y, z}: the stage-2 boss's foot contacts, written every frame by Class14AdvanceMotionAndPublishPoints (points from bones 15 and 12, strengths from the anim-cue contact code, 0/75/150/300). Read by the class-0x15 floating props at 0x00441D1C, which push a prop near any live contact; FloatingPropRowSpawn zeroes all four and Class14StateDeathA zeroes the strengths. Also the planted-foot test for the boss's own ground-follow y.

Scene fog colour, red, int 0..255 -- light-block channel 2. Read only by PushSceneFogColour (0x0040D5B0), which packs r/g/b into a D3DCOLOR for D3DRENDERSTATE_FOGCOLOR. Seeded to 0xFF by FUN_00460250.
Scene fog colour, green, int 0..255 -- light-block channel 3. See g_scene_fog_r.
Scene fog colour, blue, int 0..255 -- light-block channel 4. See g_scene_fog_r.
Accumulates rank adjustments -- PlayerTakeDamage subtracts 2 -- and UpdateDamageRank adds it in and clears it on its next pass.
motion id -> {u32 base; u32 state}, state 2 = resident
int[2], per player, written by ResolveHit: 0 = nothing, 1 = damaged and part swapped, 2 = damaged only, 3 = severed, 5 = no effect (the effect table's `2` sentinel). Result 5 scores nothing.

A bit set the screen-furniture classes own. ChapterCardInstall ORs 0x20 in -- at 0x0043436D in sub 0, and at 0x004342FA / 0x00434328 in its Boss Mode and app-state-0x0B arms before it hands over -- and clears it at 0x004348C9, after raising g_script_flags[0xF8] at 0x004348C1; BossModeChapterCardUpdate (0x00434CE7) and FUN_00434DA0 (0x00434ED6) clear it for their arms. ResultCardInstall ORs 0x10 in at 0x00434FD6 in sub 0 and clears it at 0x00435685, after g_script_flags[0xFE] at 0x0043567C. Readers stand aside while a card is up: HudDrawShutterState draws no state-4 bars while & 0x30 (0x00413BB5), HudDrawLives drops HOLD YOUR FIRE under 0x10, Class22CutsceneHoldUntilChapterCard draws only while 0x20 is clear; RegionDrawResidentSet, ScriptedHumanoidDraw, SetPiecePropDrawAndTick and St1VehicleUpdate also test 0x20. Bit 0: start press takes effect at once (PlayerTryStartPress, UpdateSceneViewAndLight, EvtActionFinishSequence21); bit 1: CommitAppState; bit 3 (0x8): EvtLoadBlockProgram. [proved]

s8[10][16]: the blocks this run entered, per scene, -1 after the last -- ResetSceneCombatState appends g_evt_block_index at g_route_count; ResetGameOnStart fills all 0x28 dwords with -1. GameOverRouteMapArm replaces it with the default route 0x0059351C when scene 0's first entry is -1 or its second is 0; RouteMapDrawTask walks it (flat, stage*16 + i). [proved]
s8: the next g_route_history entry for this scene. ResetSceneCombatState (the checkpoint opcode 0x4D) stores the block at it and -1 after it, then counts it up; ResetSceneOnEnter zeroes it. [proved]

the current rideable object. ZombieStateRideCarrier (class 0x30 state 29) adds this object's +0x40/44/48 to its own recorded spawn position every frame and leaves when the carrier raises its obj+0x34 bit 0x10000000; ZombieStateDelayedStrikeInPlace (state 32) gives up to state 10 0x14 frames after the same object raises bit 0x40000000. Distinct from g_civilian_carrier (0x009A2C88), which is class 0x10's own. THREE consumers, not two, and the third is the one that moves an actor in any state: ZombieAttachToCarrier (FUN_0045E770) seats a class-0x30 actor rigidly on this object -- position through the carrier's translate and yaw, plus the actor's own stashed local offset -- and EnemyZombieUpdate calls it every frame, before the state dispatch, for any actor whose obj+0x136C bit 0x10000000 is up (raised by EnemyZombieInitByCharType from descriptor flag bit 3). Written by ScriptedSceneryDispatch33 (00433014) in class 0x33's Init as well as by ScriptedCarrierUpdate33 (004331E1) every frame, so it is live on the same frame the carrier is made -- which is how stage 5 block 2's op-37 car is already published when op 38 spawns its four riders.
Counts frames of input: InputReadFrame adds 1 each GameFrameTick. CreditBlinkTick's source; also read by FUN_0040D290, FUN_0040E500 and FUN_0041DD00 (unread). [proved for the writer]

Frames the current screen has run: RunPhaseInPlay counts it after the task walk (0x00460244), and the other screens' routines zero and count their own -- FUN_00495EB0, TitleMenuRunPhase, RunAttractDemo, RunAttractScene10/11, NetworkModeRunPhase, FUN_0041A5E0, FUN_004996C0/FUN_004997A0, FUN_00480D90 -- as does the boot reset. CreditBlinkTick shows the attract PRESS START from its 4th frame; SetPiecePropDrawAndTick tests & 7. [proved from the xref list]
frame + 0x0C: the s16 triple array SkeletonWalkNode indexes

One of the three free-running counters FUN_0040E730 steps once a game tick, beside g_frame_counter (0x009A32A0) and g_scene_tick_counter (0x009A2BAC). The name is now too narrow and is kept only because renaming it wants a sweep: class 0x31 states 5, 27 and 34 read its low bit for a blink parity, and it is ALSO the cel phase of two per-bone draw hooks -- ZombieDrawBonePart (FUN_004534A0) reads it as g_blink_frame_counter + obj+0x3C*10 and indexes runs of 5, 18, 20, 25, 30, 50 and 120 models with it, and ThrowerDrawBonePart reads it %%0x32 and %%0x78 for the same purpose. What distinguishes it from the other two is its reset scope: LoadSceneAndReset (0x00460030) and ResetSceneCombatState (0x0045EEC0) both zero this one, where g_scene_tick_counter is zeroed only by ResetSceneOnEnter and g_frame_counter only by the new-game reset.

s16 per player, +player*0x130. The per-player shell's state, and the index into g_player_state_handlers (see there for all twelve). 5 is IN PLAY, and PlayerEnterPlay (0x00414770) is the only way to it: rows 0..3 of g_player_enter_play_modes carry it. The boot reset FUN_0040A920 writes 9 to both players (0x0040AA3D), CommitAppState writes 9 outside app states 6/7, AdvanceToNextScene parks a 5 at 2 for a scene load, PlayerUpdateInPlay sets 4 the frame the lives reach 0, and NetworkModeRunPhase (0x0049F4E4) and the Boss name-entry exit (0x00481F3C) write 0. IsPlayerAttackable requires 5, CheckPlayerCanBeHit requires 1, 4 or 5 in play, and BatDiveUpdate, BatSwarmUpdate and HordeMemberUpdate take a life only while a player is at 5. It does NOT change on being hit: the invulnerability window is g_player_invuln_frames. [proved]
+player*0x98. PlayerTakeDamage decrements it by one per strike; the continue screen restores 1 or 2.
s16 +player*0x130: the lives copy PlayerUpdateInPlay takes after its HUD draw and PlayerEnterPlay seeds beside g_player_lives. [proved]

s32 +player*0x130: the score. ScoreAddForPlayer is its writer and floors it at 0 (and doubles the points in Original Mode while 0x009A2243 is 2); PlayerEnterPlay clears it on row flag 4; FUN_00413FF0 draws it. [proved]

The player's aim in screen pixels, +player * 0x130 -- the same per-player block as g_player_lives. BuildShotRay unprojects it with g_projection_distance_px and PlayerShotEffectSpawn and SpawnPropHitSpark divide by the same number.
The other half of g_crosshair_x, +0x04.
set to 1 by the player update when the trigger is down and ammo remains; cleared by ProcessPlayerShots

s16, +player * 0x130. PlayerFireAndReloadUpdate takes one per shot and PlayerRefillMagazine puts back six, or g_player_magazine_size in Original Mode; the shot that takes it to 0 raises g_player_magazine_empty. HudDrawAmmoAndReloadPrompt draws one bullet per round.

s16 +player*0x130 (+0x1E of the per-player block): the empty latch. PlayerFireAndReloadUpdate and PlayerFireOriginalModeWeapon set it 1 (and g_player_reload_prompt_timer 0) on the shot that takes g_player_ammo to 0; PlayerRefillMagazine, PlayerReloadOriginalModeWeapon and GameFrameTick's auto-reload clear it. HudDrawAmmoAndReloadPrompt draws the RELOAD prompt only while it is set. [proved]

s16 +player*0x130: frames since the magazine ran dry. Zeroed with g_player_magazine_empty; HudDrawAmmoAndReloadPrompt steps it once a call and puts it back to 120 once it passes 600. RELOAD (0xA27) blinks on (timer % 60) < 45; from 120 the second line joins it and the dry-trigger voice changes. [proved]
+player*0x98. Added to the 120-point headshot award and then incremented by 10, so consecutive headshots pay 120, 130, 140 ...; any non-head hit zeroes it.

+player*0x98 (0x130 bytes). The accuracy denominator: EvtOpAwardAccuracyBonus2B (0x0045FE40) pays g_accuracy_bonus_table[(g_player_hit_count * 100 / this) / 10] to any player whose g_player_state is 5 and who has fired more than 0x13 shots, so this is shots and g_player_hit_count at +4 is hits. Distinct from g_nPlayerFired (0x009A5C78), which is a per-frame "the trigger is down" flag and not a tally. ResetSceneOnEnter zeroes it with the other two, so the accuracy grade is per scene. [open] No instruction writes it through this address -- the increment reaches it on a computed base the disassembler does not resolve here.
+player*0x98. Hits that scored, for the end-of-stage accuracy grade evt 0x2B reads.
s32 +player*0x130: PlayerStateArmGameOver's 0x78 frames before the player is out. [proved]
Four dwords +player*0x130 (+0x2C..+0x38): the credit counts the per-player continue countdown last saw. [proved]
s32 +player*0x130: the state a start press asked for while it waited in state 10. [proved]
s32 +player*0x130: the per-player continue countdown, 0x9FFF, -0x2D a frame, digit >> 12. [proved]

+player*0x98. Set by PlayerTakeDamage when its second argument is non-zero; read by PlayerHookSpawnDamageOverlay (spawns the damage overlay) and consumed -- cleared, starting the screen shake -- by UpdateScreenShake. CommitAppState also writes it. [proved]

+player*0x130, s16. PlayerTakeDamage's third argument, stored when its second is non-zero. Its one reader is PlayerHookSpawnDamageOverlay, which hands it to DamageOverlaySpawn as the damage overlay kind (0..10): it selects the full-screen damage sprite and its sound. Formerly named g_player_hit_motion (and the attack entry's +0x0A the 'player motion'); nothing reads it as a motion. [proved]
The player task's pointer, +player*0x130, filled by PlayerTasksCreate. [proved]
Per player (+p*0x130): the player's skinned body actor, PlayerBodiesCreate's. [proved]

Code pointer, per player (+player*0x130): the hook PlayerRunCameraHook calls every frame from PlayerUpdateInPlay. Written by the scene-state installers (PlayerHookSpawnDamageOverlay for row 2 minors 4-7, PlayerHookDrawBody for row 1 minors 1 and 2) and by FUN_00414420 / PlayerHookDrawBodyUntilMotionEnd. [proved]
s8 +player*0x130: MapleDeviceKind of a non-gun device (0 standard controller, 1, 2), -1 otherwise. PlayerInputBindingSet reads it. [proved]

s8 +player*0x130: 1 when the player's emulated maple device is a gun (flag 0x80) -- the PC MOUSE in input modes 5/6, the MC PC light gun, a joystick with bit 31 -- 0 for a standard controller (the PC keyboard), -1 for none. PlayerBindMapleDevices writes it. It picks PollPlayerAimInput's arm, PlayerFireAndReloadUpdate's reload (an off-screen shot for a gun, the binding set's reload bit otherwise) and the RELOAD prompt's second line. [proved]

Camera block +0x00, stride 0x1A4: the world-to-view matrix UpdateSceneViewAndLight builds. FishProjectToScreen writes obj+0x70 through it and CarriedPropThrowAtCamera draws through it; g_camera_blocks (0x009A6040, the block's +0x40) is its inverse, view to world -- CarriedPropRelease takes a view-space matrix to the world through that one. [proved]
per-camera blocks, stride 0x1A4

g_camera_blocks + 0x80: the eased eye position of camera block g_camera_index, a vec3 FUN_00402EF0 eases toward the pose the path evaluated. FUN_00403B00 reads it as the eye when it measures the angle to the look-at target at block+0x98 (g_camera_block_target), which is what proves the three words are a position.
g_camera_blocks + 0x8C, the camera block's X rotation. UpdateSceneViewAndLight builds the camera as T(eye) Ry(yaw) Rx(this) Rz(roll); HordeMemberUpdate's dive lifts its arc by 2*sin(this).

g_camera_blocks + 0x90, a BAMS yaw per camera block, indexed g_camera_index * 0x1A4 -- the same stride and block g_camera_block_eye (0x009A60C0, +0x80) and g_camera_block_target (+0x98) live in. VecToAngles(eye - target) (CamBlockSetAnglesFromLookAt), so it is the camera's own +z, the axis pointing back at the viewer; UpdateSceneViewAndLight builds the view T(eye) Ry(this) Rx Rz and reads it back with MatrixGetAngles every frame, inside the camera actor's task and before every other actor. NOT g_camera_yaw_bams (0x009C71F0), which the scene state's hooks write as a heading turned half round -- the rail pose's yaw + 0x8000 under (2,6)/(2,7), this - 0x8000 under (1,3)/(2,5) -- and which the port used to read in its place, half a turn out. Readers found by operand (58) and by the bytes d0609a00 (63): the camera's own routines, ZombieShouldStandAndThrow, ChooseDeathMotionDirectional, ActorHeadAimAngles, ActorFacePlayerTarget's two-player arm, ZombieStateTargetMotionScript's strip, class 0x30 state 0x34's routine at 0x0045E330 (read at 0x0045E54A), SeveredHeadUpdate, WaterSplashUpdate, OwlPickTargetPlayerAndAimOffset, OwlUpdateAndResolveShot, BatDiveUpdate, BatSwarmUpdate, CarrierPropRoutine1/6 and the unread routines 3/4/5/7/8, BreakablePropUpdate, KindedPropUpdate, PropUpdateType43, FallingContainerUpdate, the six Class14 states, Class26Subtype2Update and FUN_0048F190 (+ 0x8000), Boss3BodyUpdate and Boss3PathEffectUpdate, DrawRainParticles, DrawBackdropSlotInViewSpace (negated), ChapterCardInstall, BodyCreatureUpdate's launch (0x0043E980), and unread code at 0x004299CC, 0x0042A9CF, 0x0042B14D, 0x0042BC3C, 0x0042BF77, 0x0042C5CC, 0x0042D967, 0x00465C91, 0x0046871D/73/E2, 0x00472A89 and 0x00498058. Direct writers outside the camera: Boss3BodyUpdate (0x0042410D), CameraTaskCreateAtOrigin, TitleMenuCameraTaskCreate. [proved]

g_camera_blocks + 0x94, camera block 0's roll word. CamBlockSetAnglesFromLookAt stores its third argument here: CamAdvancePathFrame passes CamEvalPath7's roll, the hand-back routines 0, CameraTrackEnemiesTick this word back; CameraDriverFromDeferredPose copies g_cam_path_roll_bams over it. UpdateSceneViewAndLight builds the view with it. [proved]
The camera block's current look-at point (block+0xD8). StepCameraLookAtDamped eases it toward g_camera_lookat_target rather than snapping.

Slot 0 of the four 0x1A4-byte evt-action blocks: the handler for the queued action currently running. EvtRunQueuedActions is the ONLY caller -- CALL dword ptr [0x009A610C] at 0x00402323, always with argument 0 -- so slots 1..3 are written but never invoked and the 'param_1 != 0' arm of every action handler is dead. Set on dequeue; re-pointed by handlers (CamStartPathPlayback -> CamAdvancePathFrame; EvtActionFinishSequence21 -> DAT_00576B20[minor], non-null only for minors 4/6/7); parked on the bare RET FUN_0041EBB0 when the ring drains. evt 0x31/0x32 install that bare RET, which is what tears down the finish-sequence camera driver.
camera block 0's current path frame (+0xD0 of the block)

Camera block 0's +0x104: the NEXT path frame CamAdvancePathFrame will publish. g_cam_path_frame (+0xD0) is the one it published last. The publish is 'g_cam_path_frame = cursor' and happens before the 'end <= cursor' test, so the frame a path ends on IS published, and the action is retired in the same call.
Camera block 0's +0x108: the last frame of the range a cam_play asked for. CamStartPathPlayback writes it from the action's second operand, or from g_stashed_path_end_frame for a flags-and-4 play.

Camera block 2's eye, g_camera_blocks + 2*0x1A4 + 0x80, and the first of the six dwords (eye, pitch, yaw, roll) EvtRunQueuedActionsSyncViewBlock copies from block 0 (0x009A60C0) while g_scene_state_minor_entered is 3 (REP MOVSD at 0x00402431). CameraBlocksReset zeroes it; UpdateSceneViewAndLight rebuilds it every frame. Block 2 is not the view -- g_camera_index is 0 in every shipped write. [proved]
Camera block 2's X rotation, block + 0x8C. See g_camera_block2_eye. [proved]

Camera block 2's yaw, block + 0x90: CamBlockSetAnglesFromLookAt(block 2, its copied look-at, block 0's roll) at 0x00402455 during a (1,3) view-angle turn, so block 0's heading then, the last such turn's heading afterwards, or zero after CameraBlocksReset. One literal reader in the image, MOV EBP, [0x009A6418] at 0x0043AB62: FrogStateHopWithinScreenWedge's screen-edge rays (operand search and the bytes 18649a00 agree). [proved]
Camera block 2's roll, block + 0x94; the ==5 arm of EvtRunQueuedActionsSyncViewBlock reads it (0x00402407), unreachable. [proved]
Camera block 2's look-at, block + 0xD8, copied from block 0's (0x009A60D8, six dwords at 0x00402442) during a (1,3) view-angle turn. [proved]

Camera block 2's current path frame -- the same +0xD0 field again, at g_camera_blocks + 2*0x1A4. A scripted state waiting on a camera cue accepts either this or g_cam_path_frame: class 0x31 state 27 does, and so does class 0x33 at 0x00433B1A.

The copy of g_scene_state_major that only a full EvtEnterSceneState (0x00403BD0) stamps -- FUN_00403BB0 is the same routine WITHOUT this pair, so these two say a real scene-state entry happened rather than a bare table jump. **IsPlayerAttackable (0x00409DC0) reads this one and requires 2**, which is the cam/ path camera row of g_scene_state_table: enemies may only commit an attack while a scripted path camera is driving. Measured over the ports own walker, major 2 is almost all of gameplay (minors 4, 6 and 7) and major 1 minor 3 -- CameraFromViewAngles -- is the brief scripted-turn spell where nobody may attack. Also written directly by EvtOpGotoSceneState31, which sets it to 1, and by EvtOpGotoSceneStateWhenPlayersAlive32 and FUN_0040A920.
The minor half of the pair EvtEnterSceneState stamps beside g_scene_state_minor; see g_scene_state_major_entered (0x009C6F08).

The index CameraDriverSelectMode (0x00402650) writes and dispatches through g_camera_mode_hooks (0x00576CBC). 2 is CameraDispatchHandBack -- the room is clear and the aim is coming back onto the rail -- and 3 is CameraTrackEnemiesTick; 6 is PoseHookNone and 7 is 0x00402A40, both forced by overrides; 0, 1, 4 and 8 are SceneStateInvalidHang. EvtActionFinishSequence21 seeds it with 3. **It is recomputed from scratch every frame** while g_camera_hand_back_variant is not negative, which it never is, so the stored value is only ever read back on a path the shipped game does not take.

Which player may be targeted, computed by SelectAttackablePlayer from g_players_in_play: -1 nobody, 0 player 0 only, 1 player 1 only, 2 both. [proved]

byte array the evt script sets and waits on -- 0x100 bytes, zeroed by ResetSceneOnEnter (FUN_0045EDD0) and by nothing else. ONE array, written from all over the image and read from all over it. Script and gameplay share it in both directions, which is the point of it. Sweep it with the bare '9c72' and with a byte-pattern search for the little-endian address, never with '0x9c7200'. ELEMENT 12 IS THE ONE TO WATCH FOR THE SHADOW TRAP: Ghidra carries it as its own symbol DAT_009C720C, which hides that it is this array, and its three meanings have nothing to do with each other -- Class14StateSummonRoundB writes 1 into it at 0x0047A264 and scene 1 waits on it in blocks 37 and 41 (the stage-2 boss's summon gate), scene 4 raises it in block 5 step 2 to start PropDrawOnlyType54's drift, and scene 5 raises it in seven separate blocks. How many class-0x30 actors currently hold the ONE shared looping held-weapon SE. Written by EvtOpEnableEntitySpotlights15 (evt 0x15), zeroed by SceneLightArrayInit. BuildEntitySpotlightArray lights nothing unless it is exactly 1.

The firing gate. Non-zero means the player's trigger works; zero means it does nothing at all. Driven ONLY by HudDrawShutterState (evt 0x1F): set 1 in states 0, 1 and 6, set 0 in state 5 and when a state-3 close finishes counting down. ResetSceneOnEnter clears it, so a scene starts with the gate DOWN and the script must raise it. THE RULE, from PlayerFireAndReloadUpdate (0x004149BE) and its Original Mode twin FUN_00414B90 (0x00414C2D): the whole fire block sits under `else if (g_nFiringGate != 0)`, so with the gate down there is no ammo decrement, no g_player_shot_count, no BuildShotRay, no PlayerShotEffectSpawn and no gunshot sound -- the routine returns before any of it. Reload is NOT gated: both the auto-refill-when-empty path and the reload-button path run either way, and only the reload SOUND is gated (0x00414B75 in PlayerRefillMagazine, 0x00414E88 in FUN_00414E40, 0x0040E7B3 in FUN_0040E730). It also hides the HUD: the crosshair sprite HudDrawCrosshair draws only when it is non-zero (0x00416A65), and PlayerUpdateInPlay calls the ammo readout HudDrawAmmoAndReloadPrompt only when it is non-zero (0x00413F63); inside that, the RELOAD prompt is gated again (0x00418001). Finally it is the polarity of the cutscene skip: with the gate DOWN and g_nEvtSkippableRegion set, the trigger sets g_nSkipRequested instead of firing (0x00414AE2, 0x00414DF9). Five more writers exist outside the stage script -- FUN_00425E90, FUN_00497360, FUN_00497760 (all 0), FUN_00480D90 (1) -- all on top-level screens rather than in a scene; [likely] menu/result screens, not read for this.

The application state -- which of the game's top-level screens is running. Committed only by CommitAppState (0x0040E860) from the pending request at g_app_state_pending (0x007C17A0). PROVED values: 5 = the attract demo (RunAttractDemo runs only while it is 5, and it is IsPlayerAttackable's unconditional-attack override); 6 = IN PLAY -- FUN_00414FC0, the start-press-with-a-credit path, requests exactly 6, and CommitAppState leaves g_player_state alone only for 6 and 7 (if (pending < 6 || pending > 7) g_player_state = 9), so 6 and 7 are the only states with live players; 7 = the game-over/continue-expired arm (FUN_00460530 requests it when the continue countdown runs out, and FUN_00414FC0 refuses a start press while it is 7); 0x10 = BOOT -- FUN_0040E4A0 stamps it after FUN_0040A920's whole-segment reset, its one caller is the startup routine FUN_0049E4A0 that reads Hod2.ini, and the main loop FUN_0049E220 draws nothing while it holds. LIVE READS THAT TURN ON 6: ResolveHit ORs obj+0x34 |= 0xE00 when it is NOT 6 (0x00409495) and gates the 1-in-4 head pop on == 6 (0x00409741); PlaySoundId picks the plain BGM table over the _AR one when it is 6 and g_GameMode is 0; CivilianRunScript's op 0x2B runs only while it is 6. THE DISPATCHER IS AppStateDispatch (0x004608A0), one switch arm per screen, which names three of the requested-but-unnamed values: 4 is TitleMenuRunPhase, the title screen whose eight-row menu is the ONLY writer of g_GameMode that can produce 1, 2 or 3; 0x0C is FUN_004869E0, the OPTION row; 0x0F is NetworkModeRunPhase, the NETWORK row, whose state 7 sets g_app_state = 6 and g_GameMode = 0 together. That last one matters to the BGM rule above: g_GameMode == 0 is Arcade and is reached in play, so `state 6 && mode 0` picks the plain BGM table in ordinary Arcade play rather than never.
The state HudDrawShutterState last settled on: it seeds the slide counter on a change, and state 7 restores it. Written on every path except state 8.

The evt VM's yield flag, and the whole of its frame pacing. EvtInterpreterLoop runs 'do { dispatch[*pc](); } while (g_evt_yield == 0)' and does NOT clear it at entry, so: a wait handler reached with it clear sets it and returns WITHOUT testing its condition (every wait therefore costs at least one frame); on later frames it tests, and a satisfied wait clears it and advances pc, whereupon the loop keeps dispatching in the SAME frame until the next wait. Opcode 0x4E halt is nothing but 'g_evt_yield = 1' with pc unchanged (FUN_0045EFF0). The unused dispatch slots 0x00/0x2A/0x34/0x3C/0x4C point at a bare RET, which leaves the flag clear and spins the loop forever -- reaching one hangs the game.

Last frame's g_pad_held. [proved]

u16 per scene, indexed g_scene_index*2. CivilianInit increments it on the same straight line as g_civilians_seen_total (0x009A21BA) and g_civilians_alive, so it is every class-0x10 actor the scene created. Paired with g_civilians_rescued_by_scene for the end-of-stage rescue tally. ResetGameOnStart zeroes the first three dwords -- six scenes -- and ResetSceneOnEnter zeroes this scene only.

Which training lesson is being played, a byte. PROVED it is read in exactly two places and both are behind g_GameMode == 2, which is Training: PreloadScreenAssetList indexes g_preload_lists_training_by_lesson with it at event block 3, and PlaceBreakableGroup uses it to pick which members of a breakable group become one-shot targets (+0x11C = 1, asset 0x1A0F) -- set 0 takes members 2, 3, 4 and 6; set 1 takes 0, 1 and 5; set 2 takes 0 and 6; set 3 takes the same four as set 0. Those four sets are the four lessons, which closes the [open] this row carried while it was called g_prop_target_set from the belief that mode 2 was arcade. scr_training_sele.bin is the lesson-select screen; which lesson is which is still [open]. The browser port calls this global g_prop_target_set.

0x7C bytes per player: +0x04 f32 crosshair speed (0.5), +0x08 four binding sets of five pad masks (trigger, reload, fast crosshair, recentre, ?) indexed by PlayerInputBindingSet, copied from g_input_bindings_default by FUN_00401130; then the gun calibration. +0x78 is g_player_no_damage and +0x79 g_player_infinite_ammo. [proved for trigger and reload]
Byte +player*0x7C: non-zero and PlayerTakeDamage takes no life, no rank and no points. Only the factory options reset FUN_00401060 writes it (0); what else, if anything, sets it is [open].
Byte +player*0x7C, beside g_player_no_damage: non-zero and the fire paths skip the g_player_ammo decrement (the shot still fires). FUN_00401060 zeroes it; what sets it is [open].

Which of the four modes the title menu chose. PROVED 0 = Arcade, 1 = Original, 2 = Training, 3 = Boss. The enumeration is settled by TitleMenuUpdateAndSelect (0x00496960), whose confirm arm is "case 0: case 1: case 2: case 3: g_GameMode = g_title_menu_cursor", against TitleMenuRegisterSprites (0x004962C0), which registers the menu rows as ScreenSpriteRegister slots in order -- tex\arcade00/01/02 at 6..8, original_ at 9..11, traning_ at 12..14, boss_ at 15..17, then ranking_, option_, network_, exit_ -- and the handler lights the triple at (cursor+2)*3. EVERY OTHER WRITER STORES 0: TitleMenuRunPhase (0x0049626D) on entry, RunAttractScene10 (0x0041F9D0), RunAttractScene11 (0x0041FB20), RunAttractDemo (0x00426845, and the XOR ESI,ESI feeding it is at 0x0042682B) and NetworkModeRunPhase (0x0049F4D8) -- so 0 is both the default and Arcade, and 1..3 can only come from the menu. 163 references, and an operand search for 9ca08c returns the same 163, so no addressing mode is hidden (L32). CORROBORATION: ResetGameOnStart sends mode 2 to scene 6, which is trnevtbl.bin, with its block from DAT_009A2BBC, and mode 3 to scene 0 block 0x10; PreloadScreenAssetList gives mode 2 a per-block list and a per-g_training_lesson list and mode 3 a table exactly six entries wide, while 0 and 1 share the ordinary per-scene one; EvtLoadBlockProgram gives modes 2 and 3 entry step 0 and lets mode 0 fall through to 1; every Original Mode item, weapon and story-switch arm in the program tests == 1. THE PREVIOUS READING HAD 2 = arcade AND NO ARM FOR 0, which is why the one-shot target sweep in PlaceBreakableGroup and the no-score rule in BreakablePropAwardHit read as arcade behaviour when they are training behaviour.

s32, ftol(cos(frames*0x1800 BAMS) * frames). UpdateSceneViewAndLight re-aims the active camera block at (0, this, -1000) in its own Y-then-X frame, so it is a vertical nod of atan(this/1000). Written only by UpdateScreenShake and the boot reset FUN_0040A920. [proved]

How many class-0x10 civilians are in play; the condition for evt opcode 0x46 wait_scripted_actors, whose 68 sites all pass operand 0. CivilianInit raises it UNCONDITIONALLY -- the INC word ptr at 0x0048A6FE is on the straight-line fall-through with no branch around it. (It is the two counters three instructions later, 0x009A21BA and word[0x009C9100 + stage*2], that the wait word's 0x08000000 exempts; an earlier note here wrongly put that guard on this counter.) Three ways back out, all decrementing once: op 0x2C carrying 0x00080000 (CivilianRunScript 0x0048BA3C), which also stamps sub+0x04 bit 0; and two CivilianUpdate teardowns, 0x0048B003 after the remove-delay countdown and 0x0048B0AC in the off-camera branch, both skipped when that bit is set.

1 while a boss fight is on. Written by every boss class: 0x14 (0x00478369, 0x004785F2, 0x0047BB7F, 0x0047C0AE), 0x19 (0x00493970, 0x00493BFE, 0x004957CB), 0x22 (0x0049B6CF, 0x0049D507), 0x45 (MOV 1 at 0x00420FB7, MOV 0 at 0x00423457, BL at 0x00425EAB), 0x2D (0x0042842B, 0x00426EE9) and 0x32 (0x0047D04B, 0x0047D216) -- the joins write 1 and the deaths 0, per each class's reading. Its only reader is BossModeChapterCardUpdate (0x00434CF9, 0x00434D35), which runs the Boss Mode clock while it is up -- so outside Boss Mode nothing reads it. [proved] for the reader set (get_xrefs_to, 18 refs).

u16. Every rescue across the run; CivilianRunScript op 0x2C raises it beside the per-scene g_civilians_rescued_by_scene. Zeroed by ResetGameOnStart and NOT by ResetSceneOnEnter, which is what makes it a run total rather than a scene one.

HUD letterbox state 0..8; HudDrawShutterState (0x00413970) drives it and turns it into g_nFiringGate. SEVERAL things write it, not just evt 0x1F. evt 0x1F is EvtOpSetHudShutterState1F at 0x0045F392; the draw routine itself writes 2 and 4 as its own slides finish (0x00413A06, 0x00413A6F, 0x00413A91, 0x00413B01, 0x00413B32, 0x00413C68); BossIntroBannerUpdate stores 1 at 0x00437F1E; Class32StateDeathSequence at 0x00480193 and Class22FightPhase1 at 0x0049B899; and -- the one a shipped room a player must be able to shoot in depends on -- CIVILIAN SCRIPT OP 0x1B: 'MOV DL,byte ptr [ESI+0x4] / MOV byte ptr [0x009ca0f4],DL' at 0x0048BF13-0x0048BF16 in CivilianRunScript, guarded by g_app_state != 10 (0x0048BF0A). It is a BYTE store of the low byte of a dword operand and its command is two dwords long. 60 commands in the shared 136-block civilian script table run it, 30 of them 1 (open over 40 frames, gate on) and 30 of them 3 (close over 40 frames, gate off); CivilianReapplyWaitCommand (0x0048B760) does NOT re-apply it, it falls to that switch's two-dword default. Stage 1 block 1's tutorial captor is unshootable without it. ResetSceneOnEnter sets it to 5. [proved]
GameOverRunPhase's phase timer: 200 frames of fly-over, 0xB4 of logo; also the network screen's. [proved]

The material id of whatever the last collision trace hit, 0 for a miss. A side output: every caller reads it straight after its own query rather than being handed it. Class 0x31 latches it into obj+0x1350 where it lands, because 0x5A kills whatever touches it. Across the whole corpus 53 (0x35) is the commonest id at 874 quads, 5 and 55 are the wet surfaces, and 90 (0x5A) is seven quads.
